scenes.headline: How debim turns a building into text
scenes.sub: A grid, boxes and layers, compiled to IFC
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rebar! An open tool writes buildings as short text an agent can read. Here is how it works, and what it leaves out.

scenes.text: Write the building as one short record per element on a structural grid, and let deterministic code compile it and count quantities.
scenes.say: Describe each wall, beam and slab as a short record on a grid, and let ordinary code compile the model and do the arithmetic.

steps.say: At the centre is a YAML file: storeys, a grid of named axes, and elements placed on it.
An agent can write that file, then call tools that validate it, take off quantities and price them.
A compiler turns that file into a standard IFC model.
The viral claim is the other direction: an importer that squeezes an existing IFC file into that YAML.

scenes.title: The Duplex house in tokens
scenes.note: o200k tokenizer, my stand-in for the YAML
scenes.say: A sample house is about a million tokens as text. One short record per element is under thirty thousand.

left.title: In the IFC
left.say: In the IFC, a steel beam is an I-section with its property sets and a global id.

right.title: In the YAML
items: A solid box, same width and depth
right.say: After import it is a solid box of the same size, about nine times the steel, and the properties are gone.

scenes.title: How the fidelity score works
scenes.say: The fidelity number comes from a picture test.

items.say: Each element is drawn alone on a dark background.

items.text: Centre and scale each to fit
items.say: Each copy is centred and scaled to its own box, so position and size vanish.
Then count the pixels that differ. Background pixels always agree.

scenes.label: median score of an empty frame against the real element
scenes.say: So a blank frame, with no element at all, scores a median above ninety-two percent. The reported median is lower.

scenes.text: Use the YAML to author and count; to question an existing model, give the agent queries, not a lossy summary.
scenes.say: The format is a good way for an agent to write a building. For an existing model, let it query the real file.

recap: A grid and records, compiled to IFC
The pixel score barely sees shape
scenes.say: A grid and records, compiled to IFC. Import keeps boxes. The score barely sees shape.
